A0124.title: Real-Time On-Chain Rug Pull Detection
A0124.definition: Continuously collecting on-chain transactions, liquidity movements, and contract permission changes to identify Rug Pull indicators in real time through anomaly rules and risk models.
A0124.description: On-chain monitoring systems continuously collect liquidity-pool balances and lock periods, token-holder distribution, contract ownership and upgrade-permission changes, developer-address transfers, abnormal token minting, and sell restrictions. The detection engine evaluates liquidity-drop thresholds, concentration rules, privileged-function call patterns, fund flows, and address-history baselines, while correlating project age, audit status, and team-address labels to reduce single-signal errors. When combinations indicating liquidity removal, mint-and-dump activity, or permission takeover are detected, the system issues tiered alerts to exchanges, governance teams, and investors, records triggering rules, transaction hashes, and address evidence, and may initiate trading pauses, exposure limits, or manual review. Confirmed incidents are replayed to tune thresholds and models as attackers adopt gradual withdrawals or transfers across multiple addresses.
A0124.limitation: On-chain detection is affected by block-confirmation and indexing delays. Attackers may evade rules through gradual withdrawals, cross-chain transfers, address splitting, or transaction patterns that imitate normal activity. New projects also lack stable behavioral baselines and may generate false positives, while an alert cannot guarantee that transfers will be blocked before funds leave.
